messages:
jess_support: Heads up — ACME reported spike in API latency and then automatic failover to eu-west-1 even though most traffic is us-west-2. They say it started ~09:30 UTC. They pasted logs and say our dashboard shows a healthcheck failure at 09:29:58.
healthcheck-bot: Probe failed: 502 from us-west-2-probe-01 -> upstream 10.2.3.45:443 (timeout)
acme_sre: confirmation: our clients to us-west-2 saw ~400–600ms tail latency then a handful of 502s, then clients started hitting eu-west-1. No config changes on our side.
jess_support: Can we get SRE to triage? Priority high — customer impact.
sam_sre: I'm on it. First-glance: looks like our regional healthcheck marked us-west-2 as unhealthy and triggered routing fallback. I need the probe logs + which probe IPs failed. @liam_network can you pull packet loss/AS-path around 09:28–09:32?
liam_network: Pulling netflow and BGP dumps now. Quick question: is this the new healthcheck agent fleet that started rollout last week? Those use a different source IP pool.
 nora_infra: Yes — we rolled probe pool v2 on 2026-02-10, CIDR 34.200.0.0/19. Old pool was 34.210.32.0/20. I have the rollout window in deploy history.
sam_sre: Ok good. ACME attached the probe output: ```
2026-02-18T09:29:58Z healthcheck: probe us-west-2-probe-01 -> 10.2.3.45:443 502 Bad Gateway
2026-02-18T09:30:00Z healthcheck: probe us-west-2-probe-02 -> 10.2.3.45:443 200 OK
2026-02-18T09:30:07Z healthcheck: probe us-west-2-probe-01 -> 10.2.3.45:443 timeout
```

sam_sre: Two quick notes: 1) probes are per-IP independent; one probe failing shouldn't immediately flip if we have quorum configured. 2) But we've seen false positives during short BGP flaps.

liam_network: Netflow shows intermittent SYN retransmits from probe IP 34.200.5.12 at 09:29:57 -> 10.2.3.45. BGP session to provider X had route churn for ~12s at 09:29:55–09:30:07. Looks like probe v2 source IPs were momentarily blackholed.

acme_sre: That matches — timing is exact. But why did our routing policy send traffic to eu-west-1? Shouldn't failover require multiple consecutive failed healthchecks?

nora_infra: Our routing policy: region marked unhealthy after 2 failed probes within 30s window, fallback to next region. Quorum=3 probes; but because probes originate from different IPs, if the controller only saw 2 fails across agents it could mark unhealthy depending on controller aggregation logic. I'll check the aggregator logs.
sam_sre: Can we repro locally with a short blackhole? I want to validate aggregator behavior. Steps I'd try: 1) simulate probe IP blackhole for 10s 2) force a single API host to temporarily drop SYNs 3) observe healthcheck controller decision path. Anyone want to run a controlled repro on staging?
jess_support: ACME is ok with us running tests if we coordinate.
liam_network: I can simulate an AS-path withdrawal in staging by toggling a peer. Will need a 10–15 minute window.
nora_infra: I'll stand up a staging host that mirrors prod LB config and the aggregator. Will coordinate with sam.
sam_sre: Repro plan (staging):
1) Deploy probe-agent-v2 to staging pool (same CIDR)
2) Configure one target host to drop inbound SYNs for ~12s at T0 (iptables DROP on tcp dport 443)
3) Run healthcheck agents and send results to aggregator with same quorum settings (2 fails -> unhealthy)
4) Observe whether aggregator marks region unhealthy and triggers fallback. Capture controller logs with TRACE on healthcheck.

liam_network: I'll run AS-path withdraw sim at T0 to create the same packet loss profile.

nora_infra: Provisioned test host: staging-usw2-03 (10.10.3.45). Aggregator logs path: /var/log/health-agg/stream.log on staging. I'll ensure log-level TRACE.
sam_sre: Running repro now. Attaching quick snippet of controller behavior if it flips: ```
[2026-02-18T09:29:58Z] agg: probe us-west-2-probe-01 FAIL
[2026-02-18T09:29:59Z] agg: probe us-west-2-probe-02 OK
[2026-02-18T09:30:05Z] agg: region us-west-2 UNHEALTHY (2/3 fails) -> triggering fallback to eu-west-1
[2026-02-18T09:30:06Z] router: set route -> eu-west-1
```

jess_support: That's pretty close to ACME's timeline. Does the controller treat probes from the new pool differently? Could we have a bug where probe-v2 times out faster?

nora_infra: I checked the code: probe agent v2 uses a 2s connect timeout vs v1's 3s. We lowered it to detect blackholes faster. That could make transient blips look worse. Oops.

sam_sre: So combination: shorter timeout + BGP churn = more fails recorded -> aggregator flips region unhealthy after 2 fails. That explains the failover.

liam_network: We should also confirm our router fallback had correct cooldown so we don't oscillate. Router had no cooldown set for cross-region fallback on this config; it was relying purely on aggregator. We should add a 30s cooldown before routing changes.

acme_sre: For ACME, main ask is: can you suppress the failover and bring traffic back to us-west-2? Right now many of our clients keep hitting eu-west-1 and see >200ms RTT.

sam_sre: Short term: we can manually flip routing back to us-west-2 and pin for 10 minutes. I'll coordinate with nora to ensure we don't immediately oscillate.

nora_infra: Manual route change done at 09:35:12Z — pinned to us-west-2 for 10m. Monitoring: healthcheck aggregator still seeing occasional fails but most OK.

jess_support: ACME confirmation: they see traffic returning to us-west-2 and latency normalizing. :relieved: They asked what permanent fix will be.
sam_sre: Action items:
- nora: revert probe-v2 timeout to 3s or make it adaptive (PR #452).
- infra: add 30s routing cooldown in router policy (PR #453).
- liam: work with network provider to reduce BGP churn; escalate if recurring.
- sam: add a short circuit in aggregator to require fails from majority of agent pools (not just count) before marking region unhealthy (PR #454).

nora_infra: I'll open PR for probe-agent change and link tests. Plan: run canary with 3s timeout for two days.

liam_network: Provider called — they had a planned maintenance causing transient route flap; they didn't mark as impacting us but it did. I'll request postmortem with them.

acme_sre: Thanks for the quick response. They want a note on what happened so they can update their incident.
jess_support: I'll send a post-incident summary to ACME with timeline and action items.
sam_sre: Follow-ups: I'll paste repro run logs into the incident ticket and attach aggregator traces. If we want, we can also add a synthetic canary that runs cross-region latency checks so we detect increased cross-region traffic sooner.
jess_support: Marking as resolved for now. Reopen if ACME sees regression. :white_check_mark:
